candidate.answer:
**Partial answer — points supported by the documentation:**

- Tracing records agent/app activity; evaluations measure performance against curated test cases; Signals score agent turns and apply tags and ratings to surface problems. [S2][S4]
- Weave gives visibility into agent sessions and multi-turn conversations or individual function calls; agent traces appear on the Agents page, weave.op calls on the Traces page, and both can be used in one project but produce separate traces. [S4][S6]
- Evaluations define metrics with scoring functions, compare evaluations across metrics and samples, track which model and prompt versions produced which performance, and benchmark/monitor performance. [S3]
- The Signals tab in the Agents view shows tags and ratings for agent conversations, flagging quality and safety problems (low-quality responses, frustrated users, NSFW) and highlighting traces needing attention. [S2]
- Creating a weave.Evaluation automatically enables its scorers as Signals for every agent turn. [S3]

claims.text: Tracing records agent/app activity; evaluations measure performance against curated test cases; Signals score agent turns and apply tags/ratings to surface problems.

Weave gives visibility into agent sessions or function calls; agent traces go to the Agents page, weave.op calls go to the Traces page, and the two approaches can share a project but produce separate traces.
Evaluations define metrics with scoring functions, compare evaluations across metrics and samples, track model/prompt versions, and benchmark/monitor performance.
The Signals tab in the Agents view shows tags and ratings for agent conversations and flags quality and safety issues (low-quality responses, frustrated users, NSFW content).
Creating a weave.Evaluation automatically enables its scorers as Signals for every agent turn.

issues: The final bullet says creating a weave.Evaluation automatically turns its scorers into Signals for every agent turn. S3 does not say this, and no supplied passage describes such an automatic link. S5 (not cited) only says production traffic can be scored with the same scorers used in evaluation. Remove the bullet, or replace it with S5's cited, unqualified wording.
Revise partial or unsupported material claims.

metrics.scope: Standard Claude API list-price estimate for returned usage, including planning and verification. Excludes Weave Signals, offline evaluation judges, voice, hosting, taxes, and any usage not returned after failures or SDK/provider retries. Calls count application invocations, not every HTTP attempt. This is not an invoice. Research counts do not measure factual completeness.

budget.scope: Returned agent and judge usage at dated standard API prices. Conservative reservations before requests; SDK retries disabled by experiment adapters. Stops on unpriced usage or failed provider calls. Excludes Signals, hosting, taxes and unreturned charges. This is not an account billing cap.
